chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:
Regarding the man who is praying in a place, then intends to move forward: He should cease recitation while walking until he reaches the place he intends, then he should recite.
ai.seo_question: What should a person do with Quran recitation if they need to walk forward during prayer?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) addresses the practical etiquette of movement during prayer, emphasizing that recitation is tied to the state of standing still rather than mere presence in the prayer space. In Shia jurisprudence, this highlights the distinction between *qiyam* (standing) as a static act of devotion versus transitional movement, ensuring the integrity of the recitation is maintained by pausing it during the act of walking. This reflects the broader principle that specific pillars of prayer require specific physical conditions to be valid.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>

having said regarding the man who is praying Salāt in a place, then he intends to move forward’. Heasws said: ‘He should pause from the recitation during his walking until he goes forwards to the place which he intended to, then he should recite’.
en.sarwar: 24. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

a man may stand up in a certain place to perform Salah (prayer). He then wants to move forward. He in such case stops reading when he is walking forward, until he reaches the place that he wants, then reads.’”
